lines.en: All of the bad things in all of the world are not unfortunate coincidences nor byproducts of the timelines we find ourselves in.
They are the divine retribution of comedic false gods who only exist during times in which we’re forced to call upon them to solve problems we simply can not.
But those calls are met with laughter.
And that laughter not only pierces the innermost sections of our ears but drills holes into our skulls so wide and so malformed that we can’t help but focus on them for far longer than we should.
Not just to live and breathe and walk...but to think and hear and see.
If it were not for these comedies and the entertainment of anthropomorphized xoana who take on life only when looked at, things would be far too simple.
Gods can not exist if there is no one there to scorn them, just as I can not exist if there is no one here to scorn me.
And to think that just moments ago I seriously contemplated praying.

Another wooden idol inside another glass case somewhere- staring back at me with hollow sockets where its eyes should be? Immortalized by a small plaque and more locks than necessary to guard a piece of wood?
We could not capture gods, so we created our own.
We gave them stories and names and, in turn, lives.
But once those lives became too powerful they took everything from us, and now I can’t even walk a block down the fucking street without subconsciously damning them for their poor sense of humor.
This was not meant to happen.
I should be the one still lost.
Ayane and Maya should be the ones embracing on top of the school rooftop...and me?
I should be locked in a box.
I should be locked in a box and only taken out to be glanced over and mocked, rather than being the one who holds the key to unlock all of the boxes in-
: So...is there anywhere you think we should go first?
: I figured the shrine might be a good idea. It would probably be best to check the places Maya regularly visits before doing anything else.
: I think we should go back to the dorms.
: The dorms?...But I already told you I checked there. No one was left in any of the rooms.
: Even if we don’t find Maya, I think there might be something that could give us some sort of hint.
: A hint? Like...a note or something?
: If she’s not there, we can check the shrine. I’m just feeling a little too pissed off at the gods right now to grace them with my presence.
: We’ll find her...don’t worry. Getting mad at the gods probably isn’t going to do us any favors right now.
: I don’t blame you for feeling that way, though. Even I’m a little mad right now, and I barely ever get angry.
: Well, you should. Anger is good for you. Kind of.
: Just don’t get angry at me.
: I don’t know, Sensei...In fact, if there’s anyone I should have a reason to be mad at right now, it’s you.
: Here we are, basically dating, and I find out you’re in love with one of my best friends. That seems like a good reason to get angry, doesn’t it?
: I’m not in love with anyone, Ayane...
: I didn’t mean it like that.
: Do you want to know what I think, Sensei?
: Sure. It would be nice to learn a little more about you during our last days on earth.
: I think the problem is that you just don’t understand love.
: What I was going to say next is that not understanding love doesn’t mean you don’t feel it.
: I know for a fact you love me. And Ami. And Maya. And probably a bunch of other girls too.
: And while I’d definitely prefer a monogamous relationship, I’m not going to fault you for the things you feel, even if you can’t put those feelings into words.
: Especially because I also think that, one day...you’ll figure that part out.
: And that all of those things you tell yourself about how you’re not meant to love or be loved will sound flat out silly.
: I don’t know if I’ll be the one with you when you figure it out...or if it will be someone like Maya instead...
: But I hope you’ll get to accept and understand what it means to be in love one day.
: Because it really is the greatest feeling in the world.

Despite still not understanding the rationale, Ayane doesn’t put up a fight when it comes to heading over to the dorms- especially since it will finally give her an opportunity to change out of her pajamas.
And while I don’t expect to find Maya there given that the place has already been searched once, having some sort of...starting point might help in locating her.
And if there are any of those mystery boxes left in her room, I’ll finally be able to open one up without facing any immediate consequences.
It’s just unfortunate that it took her disappearance and the slow realization that I might not ever see her again for me to be able to do that.
Memories are silly, the way they come and go.
And nostalgia’s like a blanket of softest, whitest snow.
But winter’s dead, the snow is gone, and all that’s left is woe.
So if my memories are next to die, you can say I told you so.
: So...what is it we’re looking for again? A...note or something?
: Maya keeps a bunch of sketchy boxes near the foot of her bed that I think might have some sort of...hint or something in them.
: At least that’s the only logical conclusion I can draw at the moment pertaining to why she always has me carry them to the school in the middle of the night.
: Also, we were just at the school. Why didn’t you look while we were there?
: Easy. I didn’t think of it until we were already halfway here.
: Sensei, I love you, but for both of our sakes, I really hope you get better at this whole “end of the world” thing.
: Hey, don’t take it out on me just because you’re weirdly cool and comfortable with all of this.
: I’m not comfortable at all. I’m horrified.
: It’s just that being next to you makes that okay.
: And that as long as you don’t leave my sight again for the rest of our lives, I’ll be fine.
: Right. Well, on that note, it’s time we get to searching.
: Come on, Ayane. If we’re going to the shrine after this, we need to-
: I guess I can start by checking on the kotatsu for any notes she may have left if you want to start going through her boxes.
: Oh, and I’ll handle going through her clothes and her pockets and stuff since I’m not really comfortable with the idea of-
: She’s right there on the bed.
: Hey, if...if this is some kind of joke...it’s not really funny, Sensei. I’m already scared enough.
: Do you really not see her?
YOUR TRANSGRESSIONS CLING TO THE WALLS OF THIS ROOM LIKE SMOKE
THAT WHICH YOU HAVE DEFILED APPEARS BEFORE YOU BUT NO ONE ELSE
IS THIS THE LIFE OF PRIZES YOU HAVE WISHED FOR???
TELL ME HOW IT FELT TO BE ROOTED TO THE GROUND
TELL ME THE THINGS YOU THINK OF WHEN YOU GO TO SLEEP AT NIGHT
I WANT TO KNOW EVERYTHING ABOUT YOU
SO VERY VERY VERY VERY VERY VERY VERY VERY INTERESTED
I WILL BE IGNORED NO LONGER
TOUCH THESE CALLOUSED HANDS THAT REACH FOR YOU AND ONLY YOU
OPEN YOUR EYES AND LET IN THE NIGHT
YOU CAN SEE THE THINGS THAT THEY CAN NOT
: Sensei...maybe we should just go to the shrine now? It’s clear you’re not feeling well and-
: Sensei, please! This is getting really, really weird!
Maya lies on the bed, brow furrowed and twitching every seven seconds as the chemicals dancing around in the deepest parts of her brain cause her to see things I can not see myself.
Behind me is another girl, now on the verge of breaking into tears as I speak to someone I can see but she can not.
I wonder to myself if this is what it’s like for everyone.
If every other bed has another sleeping girl inside of it and that no one has disappeared at all.
But I am too absorbed in the prospect of saving this one to check on any of the others.
I have to save her so I can fix her.
I have to fix her because that is my job.
I have to fix her because she needs to be fixed.
: H-Here! I’ll even open the box for you! It’s-
: Sensei, come look at this. This box has-
: You’re supposed to be on the roof right now.
: Sensei, seriously. I think this might actually-
I reach out and touch her.
: Oh, Maya! You’re back early. I thought you went to take a shower?
: Sensei was just going over the Japanese homework with me since that’s the only thing you’re actually better than me at.
: You’re free to join in but, like you said earlier, I am “annoying and intrusive,” so I would understand if you want to sit this out and study on your own.
: I’m only going to be here for an hour today, though. So if you’re not going to join in, please let me have Sensei to myself and you can get him back once my mom comes to pick me up.
: What the fuck is going on here?
: I mean what the fuck is going on here?!
: Woah. Calm down there, cranky-pants. I always have lessons at this time. Just because you don’t like me doesn’t mean I’m going to stop coming.
: I do not give a shit about you, Noriko! I want to know how I got here! How is this happening?!
: You probably just...walked or something? How am I supposed to know how you got here?
: I don’t understand what you’re saying.
: I’m telling you I don’t fucking understand! I don’t understand any of this!
: You’re not real! Neither of you are real! None of this is fucking real!
: Maya, come on. Do you really have to start getting existential now of all times? I already told you that I’m only here for an hour today.
: I get that we’re the gifted kids and stuff, but you really need to lay off all of those weird “Nothing is real” monologues if you’re ever going to make it anywhere in life.
: There’s no way I’m actually back...right?
: This is a dream. This is all just a dream.
: You’re not him. You can’t be. I don’t believe it.
: None of this is actually happening. Any minute, I’m going to wake up...and I’m going to go back to the roof, and I’m going to see him and...
: And he’s going to look at me. The real me. The one that grew up.
: The one that stopped coming here as soon as you did. The one that’s followed you all this time.
: You’re not him. There’s no way you’re him.
: But then why does this hurt so fucking much?!
: I am telling you...I do not fucking get it.
: STOP USING HIS FUCKING VOICE! YOU HAVEN’T EARNED IT!
: YOU HAVEN’T BEEN THROUGH WHAT HE’S BEEN THROUGH! WHAT WE HAVE BEEN THROUGH!
: No! No no no no no no no no no no!
: Send me back! I want to go back!
: This is not what I wished for!
: What?! What are you trying to say to me in that stolen fucking voice?!
: Again, I can’t fucking understand you!
: Get the fuck out of here, Noriko! The last person I want showing up in my nightmares is fucking you!
: Nightmares? Wait, do you think you’re dreaming right now? Is that why you’re so cranky today?
: Maya, Sensei is trying to tell you to-
: SHUT THE FUCK UP! I DON’T NEED YOUR HELP!
: Oh, I know that. You’ve never needed my help before.
: In fact, you’ve never needed anyone’s help before, right? At least that’s what you’re always saying.
: But we both know that deep down, you’re basically begging to be coddled and-
: Oh, right. Sorry, Sensei. I’ll wait my turn and let Maya finish getting this little temper tantrum out of her system before we pick back up.
: A life trapped inside of this room without the one thing in it that managed to keep me sane?
: Is this what I get for defying God?
: Is this what I get for falling in love?!
: Fuck you! Fuck you, fuck you, fuck you! Send me back! Send me back right now!
